🌟 GarmentCode | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Designing and generating parametric sewing patterns for customizable garments.
✨ Key Features: • Modular programming framework for parametric sewing patterns • PyGarment core library with base types and operators • Design of garment components and interfaces • Support for body measurements and design presets • Online configurator demo (GUI)
📖 Summary: GarmentCode is a Python framework for designing parametric sewing patterns. It provides a library (PyGarment) for defining garment components and their relationships, enabling the creation of customizable and adaptable clothing designs. The project also includes a dataset of 3D garments and a configurator GUI for interactive design.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 effectcraft | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: Creating motion graphics, visual effects, and animated titles.
✨ Key Features: • Motion graphics and compositing tool • Rust implementation • After Effects-like interface and behavior • Lottie import and export • Readable JSON project files
📖 Summary: EffectCraft is an open-source motion graphics and compositing tool written in Rust, aiming to be a clean-room reimplementation of Adobe After Effects. It offers features like Lottie import/export, scriptability, and a readable project file format, making it suitable for creating animated titles, motion graphics, and visual effects.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 pipedream | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Building event-driven automations and integrating disparate applications through a low-code platform with custom code capabilities.
✨ Key Features: • Workflows: Sequences of steps (pre-built actions or custom code) triggered by events. • Event Sources: Triggers for workflows, emitting events from services like GitHub, Slack, and Airtable.
📖 Summary: Pipedream is a developer-focused integration platform that enables the creation of event-driven automations by connecting various applications. It offers pre-built components for over 1,000 integrations and supports custom code in Node.js, Python, Golang, and Bash for complex logic.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ jarm | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Identifying and grouping TLS servers on the internet based on their unique TLS configurations, with applications in security, infrastructure analysis, and threat detection.
✨ Key Features: • Active TLS server fingerprinting • Generates unique JARM fingerprints • Verifies TLS configuration consistency • Groups servers by TLS configuration
📖 Summary: JARM is a Python-based tool for active Transport Layer Security (TLS) server fingerprinting. It generates unique fingerprints for TLS servers by analyzing their responses to a series of Client Hello packets, enabling verification of TLS configurations, grouping of servers by configuration, identification of default infrastructure, and detection of malicious command and control servers.
